title: Workload Stitcher and Quant Signature Presets
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduces workload stitching and quant-signature presets to provide conservative, workload-aware defaults for batching, caching, and quantization profiles. Improves unit-econ estimates in the Console and adds guardrails/fallbacks to preserve quality.
body:
Summary: Add a "workload stitcher" component and a compact "quant signature" preset format to automatically pick conservative batching/caching/quantization defaults for production workloads. This PR wires the stitcher into the serving runtime and Console recommendations so teams get reasonable unit-econ defaults without manual tuning.

Motivation and context: Many customers ask for safe default policies that lower token cost while preserving P99 latency and quality. Previous autotune efforts were either too aggressive for some tail workloads or required heavy profiling. The stitcher groups requests by lightweight workload fingerprints and applies curated presets (batching, cache TTLs, quant signatures) to each group. Presets are intentionally conservative with an opt-in pathway for aggressive tuning.

What this PR does (single-string description): Adds a runtime "stitcher" that computes workload fingerprints (model, prompt shape, route tags), matches them against a small presets catalog, and outputs a decision payload used by the batching layer and the quant-loader. Implements a compact "quant signature" schema (name/version, supported ops, recommended quant bits, fallback policy) and several curated presets targeting common web-search, chat, and short-prompt workloads. Exposes the stitcher decisions to Console via the /v1/internal/workload-decisions API and augments the unit-econ estimator to include per-preset expected token cost reduction and estimated latency impact. Adds tests, docs, and an integration test that runs the stitcher against recorded trace samples.

Checklist: - [x] Runtime stitcher implementation (src/runtime/stitcher.py + tests) - [x] Quant signature schema and presets (configs/econ-presets/*.yaml) - [x] Console wiring: decisions endpoint + UI tip (console/api/workloads.go, console/static/workload-tips.md) - [x] Unit-econ estimator updates (tools/econ/estimator.py) - [x] Integration test with recorded traces (tests/integration/test_stitcher_end_to_end.py) - [x] Documentation and an RFC-style design note (docs/rfc/workload-stitcher.md) - [x] Small migration to load presets via configmap in Private installer (installer/k8s/presets-configmap.yaml)

Commits (high level): - Add workload stitcher skeleton and unit tests - Implement quant signature format and loader; add presets for chat/search/short-prompt - Wire stitcher output into batching decision path and KV-cache heuristics - Console: add endpoint and simple UX hint linking to docs - Integration tests + recorded trace harness + CI flakiness fixes

Files changed (high level): - src/runtime/stitcher.py (new): core matching logic and fingerprinting - src/runtime/batcher.py (mod): accepts stitcher decision payload to choose batch size/timeout - src/runtime/quant_loader.py (mod): load quant signature presets and observe fallback policy - configs/econ-presets/chat-conservative.yaml (new)
- configs/econ-presets/search-short.yaml (new) - tools/econ/estimator.py (mod): estimate unit-econ delta per preset - console/api/workloads.go (mod): internal endpoint returning recent decisions - docs/rfc/workload-stitcher.md (new) - tests/unit/test_stitcher.py, tests/integration/test_stitcher_end_to_end.py

Design notes and constraints: - Presets are intentionally conservative: the default quant bit recommendation errs toward lower compression when SLO/quality impact is uncertain. - Stitcher fingerprint is stable for small prompt format changes and uses hashed (non-PII) features only. - The runtime honors explicit route-level overrides and project-level opt-outs. - Fallbacks: if quant-loader fails to apply a preset (unsupported op), the runtime falls back to model's default weights (no quant) and emits a warning metric. - The Console shows expected cost delta but marks the estimate as a "guide".

Testing and CI: Initial CI run had a flaky integration test on the recorded-trace harness (timeout on CI runner). Added a backoff + deterministic seed to the harness; rerun passed all checks. CI summary: build: pass, unit-tests: pass, integration-tests: pass, lint: pass, e2e-sim: pass.

Review conversation (high-level transcript): Marco Li (reviewer): "Nice approach. Two asks: add a metric for \"stitcher-miss-rate\" and tighten the comment about fingerprint privacy. Also please add a simple perf benchmark comparing latency for 1k qps with/without stitcher."
Aisha (author): "Added stitcher-miss-rate metric and expanded privacy comment. Added the microbenchmark script under tools/bench/stitcher_bench.py and included results in the RFC."
Sanjay Rao (reviewer): "We should not expose presets to non-admin users by default in Private installer. Confirmed presets are loaded into a configmap that admins can edit; please add a note to the installer README."
Aisha: "Installer README updated; presets are off by default and require enabling the 'econ-presets' feature flag for Private installs."
Elena Ortiz (reviewer): "Tests look good. One nit: make the console tip copy shorter and link to the RFC. Approving after nit."
Aisha: "Addressed nit; shortened UI copy and linked RFC."

Approvals: Marco Li: approved after updates. Sanjay Rao: approved. Elena Ortiz: approved.

CI workflow notes and flakiness history: First CI run (2024-11-06) failed on tests/integration/test_stitcher_end_to_end.py due to timeout in recorded-trace replay. Root cause: non-deterministic sleep in harness. Fix: seed control + fixed sleep scaling; second run (2024-11-07) fully green.

Migration / rollout plan: - Presets deployed as a configmap in hosted clusters behind feature flag "econ-presets" for 1 week Canary (10% of routes). - Monitor stitcher-miss-rate, preset-fallback-rate, per-preset unit-econ improvement, and quality-regressions (prompt-based evals). - If regressions observed, can disable per-preset via Console or revert configmap.

Backward compatibility: No breaking API changes. The new /v1/internal/workload-decisions endpoint is internal-only and gated by RBAC. Existing routing codepaths are preserved if the stitcher is disabled.

Follow-ups and TODOs (not in this PR): - Add an automatic safe-rollout policy that gradually increases aggressiveness based on eval signals (future PR). - Add an allowlist of customer-curated presets exposed in Console (UX work). - Explore learned presets via a separate ML service (research).

Merge: Squash-and-merge after approvals and green CI (merged 2024-11-12).

Notes for release notes: This change introduces an opt-in workload-safety layer that recommends conservative batching, cache, and quantization defaults using curated presets. Customers will see Console tips and an internal decisions endpoint; admins can control presets via configmap.

If you want to run local integration: see docs/rfc/workload-stitcher.md -> "Local dev guide" section for step-by-step instructions and sample trace bundles to replay.
